t:
Section 133(d) of title 23, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:


“(5) 
Applicability of certain requirements to third party sellers.—

“(A) 
In general.—Except as provided in subparagraphs (B) and (C), in the case of a transportation enhancement activity funded from the allocation required under paragraph (2), if real property or an interest in real property is to be acquired from a qualified organization exclusively for conservation purposes (as determined under section 170(h) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986), the  organization shall be considered to be the owner of the property for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 4601 et seq.).


“(B) 
Federal approval prior to involvement of qualified organization.—If Federal approval of the acquisition of the real property or interest predates the involvement of a qualified organization described in subparagraph (A) in the acquisition of the property, the organization shall be considered to be an acquiring agency or person as described in section 24.101(a)(2) of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970.


“(C) 
Acquisitions on behalf of recipients of federal funds.—If a qualified organization described in subparagraph (A) has contracted with a State highway department or other recipient of Federal funds to acquire the real property or interest on behalf of the recipient, the organization shall be considered to be an agent of the recipient for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to a "qualified organization", its "involvement", and "Federal approval" show an outside party taking part in a federal decision. But the section only defines the legal status of a conservation organization (owner, acquiring agency, or agent) under the Uniform Relocation Act when it sells or acquires property. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: the organization shall be considered to be an agent of the recipient for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970

qwen_block.w: This section defines the legal status of qualified organizations (non-profits) for the purpose of applying federal relocation and acquisition laws. It determines whether they are treated as owners, acquiring agencies, or agents. It does not require the federal government to consult with these organizations, hold public hearings, or include them in advisory bodies before making a decision. It is a definitional provision regarding regulatory applicability, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: the organization shall be considered to be the owner of the property for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970

opus.w: This section only decides how qualified conservation organizations are treated under the Uniform Relocation Act: as the owner, as an acquiring agency, or as an agent of a funding recipient. It is tempting to read it as participation because it names outside parties and mentions contracts and Federal approval. But none of these outside parties are consulted, heard or allowed to object before a federal decision, and nothing requires a comment period, a hearing or rulemaking.
opus.s: the  organization shall be considered to be the owner of the property for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970
opus.b:
I don't think this section requires or recommends participation.

The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions outside parties (conservation organizations and State highway departments), contracts, and "Federal approval." But it only decides how those organizations are classified under the Uniform Relocation Act: as the owner, as an acquiring agency, or as an agent of the funding recipient. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the legal status of qualified organizations (non-profits) when they acquire property on behalf of federal fund recipients. It treats them as agents or owners for the purpose of applying relocation assistance laws. This is a procedural definition regarding the administration of grants and contracts, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. The definition excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text falls under that exclusion as it governs the mechanics of funded activities.
qwen_chat.s: If a qualified organization described in subparagraph (A) has contracted with a State highway department or other recipient of Federal funds to acquire the real property or interest on behalf of the recipient, the organization shall be considered to be an agent of the recipient for the purpose of the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because "qualified organizations" (non-profits) are involved in acquiring property, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." This section defines the legal status of these organizations for the purpose of federal funding and relocation assistance rules. It does not require the federal government to consult with these organizations before making a decision; rather, it dictates how the government treats them *after* they have been selected or contracted to perform a specific task (acquisition). The involvement is transactional/contractual, not advisory or consultative in the context of policy decision-making.
